ONE-PAGER.html.title: MCP Server: Code Analysis & Automated Fixes | RoselineMCP
ONE-PAGER.html.summary:
MCP Server: Code Analysis & Automated Fixes Tagline: Let AI run safe, scripted code cleanups on your C# repos and hand you a review‑ready patch. Problem Teams want automated help to surface code smells and apply proven fixers, but they need guardrails: no arbitrary edits, deterministic outputs, and developer‑controlled review (patches/PRs). Solution An MCP server exposing code‑quality tools powered by Roslyn analyzers & code fix providers and diffed with DiffPlex. AI clients (Copilot/agents) can: analyze a solution, list diagnostics by rule, and apply selected fixers; receive a unified diff patch to review in Git or apply locally. Core Tools (MCP) AnalyzeSolution(pathOrGit, branch?, include?, exclude?, severity?, maxDiagnostics?) Input: repo path or Git URL (read‑only clone), filters. Output: solution summary, per‑project counts, top diagnostics with {project, file, line, id, severity, message}. ListDiagnostics(project, ids?, files?, max?) Input: project name or path; optional rule filters. Output: diagnostics list + stats (by ID/severity), suggested fixable IDs. ApplyFixes(project, ids[], previewOnly?) Input: rule IDs to fix (e.g., ["RCS1213","SA1101"]). Behavior: creates a temporary workspace, applies available Roslyn code fixes, formats. Output: { changedFiles[], patch, fixersApplied[], notes[] } (patch is unified diff). CreatePatch(before, after) Input: two text blobs. Output: unified diff (DiffPlex) for downstream tooling. NuGet Dependencies Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp (Roslyn) Roslynator.Analyzers or StyleCop.Analyzers (rules) DiffPlex (unified diffs) Optional: Microsoft.Build.Locator (load .sln reliably), LibGit2Sharp (read‑only clone when pathOrGit is a URL) Architecture (at a glance) MCP boundary: Validates tool inputs → spins up ephemeral workspace. Analyzer host: Loads solution via MSBuildLocator → runs analyzers → collates diagnostics. Fix engine: Maps rule IDs → available CodeFixProviders → applies fixes deterministically. Diff stage: Compares original vs fixed tree → generates unified diff with DiffPlex. Return: Never mutates user repo; returns a patch + metadata. Client ⇄ MCP Tools → Analyzer Host (Roslyn) → Fix Engine → DiffPlex → Patch Security & Guardrails Read‑only by default: local copy or read‑only Git clone; no script execution. Allowlist analyzers/fixers: only vetted packages and rule IDs. Resource caps: per‑request time/CPU/file count limits; max diff size. Path sandboxing: block traversal outside workspace; redact secrets in diffs. Determinism: pinned package versions; no network during analysis. Example Flow AnalyzeSolution("https://github.com/org/app.git", branch:"main") Agent proposes: fix RCS1213, SA1101. You confirm. ApplyFixes(project:"App.Core", ids:["RCS1213","SA1101"], previewOnly:true) Server returns patch + changedFiles. You apply or open a PR. Example Schemas (JSON) AnalyzeSolution → Response (abridged) { "solution": "App.sln", "projects": 12, "diagnosticSummary": {"error": 3, "warning": 148, "info": 22}, "topDiagnostics": [ {"project":"App.Core","file":"Services/UserSvc.cs","line":87, "id":"RCS1213","severity":"warning", "message":"Remove unused parameter 'token'"} ] } ApplyFixes → Response (abridged) { "fixersApplied": ["RCS1213","SA1101"], "changedFiles": ["Services/UserSvc.cs","Controllers/AuthController.cs"], "patch": "--- a/Services/UserSvc.cs
+++ b/Services/UserSvc.cs
@@ ...
- public Task DoThing(string token)
+ public Task DoThing()
" } Operational Notes Language: C# (solution & project files). VB/FS not targeted in v1. Scale: Use per‑project batching to handle large solutions; cap diagnostics. CI usage: Run as a service; agent requests a patch → CI validates → PR. Success Metrics Warnings reduced per run; mean time to review a patch; % patches merged without edits; build/test pass rate after fixes. Roadmap (short) Fix‑All (solution‑wide) with chunked diffs PR creation (Octokit) as optional, still returning patch for review Opt‑in formatting pass (dotnet‑format) as a final step Result: A safe, repeatable way for AI to propose code improvements, while you stay in control via reviewable patches.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.html.summary: RoselineMCP Architecture Documentation Overview RoselineMCP is built on a layered architecture that separates concerns and promotes testability, maintainability, and extensibility. The system uses dependency injection throughout and follows SOLID principles. Architecture Diagram ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ MCP Client (Claude, etc.) │ └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │ stdio (JSON-RPC) ┌─────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │ MCP Server Layer │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Tool Registration │ │ │ │ (WithToolsFromAssembly()) │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Tools Layer │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ AnalysisTools │ [McpServerTool] Attributes │ │ │ │ - AnalyzeSolution │ │ │ │ - ListDiagnostics │ │ │ │ - ApplyFixes │ │ │ │ - CreatePatch │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │ Dependency Injection ┌─────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Service Layer │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Business Logic Services │ │ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ • SolutionAnalyzerService │ │ │ │ • CodeFixService │ │ │ │ • DiagnosticFilterService │ │ │ │ • CodeFixProviderFactory │ │ │ │ • PatchService / DiffService │ │ │ │ • MSBuildService │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │ External Dependencies │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ • Roslyn (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.*) │ │ │ │ • MSBuild (Microsoft.Build.*) │ │ │ │ • Roslynator (Analyzers & CodeFixes) │ │ │ │ • DiffPlex (Diff Generation) │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Core Components 1. Program.cs - Application Entry Point Responsibilities: Host configuration and startup Service registration via DI MCP server configuration Global exception handling Logging configuration Key features: Uses Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting for application lifecycle Configures stderr logging to avoid stdio conflicts Registers all services as singletons for performance Sets up environment-specific configurations 2. Tool Layer Location: Tools/ The tool layer provides the bridge between MCP protocol and internal services. Tool Registration Tools are automatically discovered using: services.AddMcpServer() .WithStdioServerTransport() .WithToolsFromAssembly(); Tool Implementation Pattern [McpServerTool] [Description("Tool description")] public static async Task<string> ToolMethod( IService1 service1, // Injected automatically IService2 service2, // Injected automatically [Description("...")] string userParam1, [Description("...")] string? userParam2 = null) { // Services are injected before user parameters // Return JSON response } 3. Service Layer Location: Services/ and Interfaces/ Core Services SolutionAnalyzerService Analyzes C# solutions and projects Collects diagnostics from Roslyn compilation Filters and aggregates results Manages MSBuildWorkspace lifecycle CodeFixService Applies automated code fixes Manages code fix providers Generates before/after patches Handles multi-file fixes DiagnosticFilterService Filters diagnostics by severity, ID, and file patterns Determines fixable diagnostics Project inclusion/exclusion logic Severity prioritization CodeFixProviderFactory Dynamically loads code fix providers Caches provider instances Maps diagnostic IDs to fixers Supports Roslyn and Roslynator providers MSBuildService Creates MSBuildWorkspace instances Manages MSBuild locator Handles workspace configuration Ensures proper cleanup PatchService / DiffService Generates unified diff patches Line-by-line diff computation Supports side-by-side and inline diffs Handles large file comparisons 4. Model Layer Location: Models/ Data transfer objects (DTOs) for structured communication: Request Models: Parameters for tool operations Response Models: Structured results from operations Domain Models: Internal representations of diagnostics, fixes, etc. Design Patterns Dependency Injection All services are registered in the DI container and injected where needed: services.AddSingleton<ISolutionAnalyzerService, SolutionAnalyzerService>(); services.AddSingleton<ICodeFixService, CodeFixService>(); // ... etc Benefits: Testability through interface mocking Loose coupling between components Easy service replacement/decoration Lifetime management Repository Pattern (Implicit) Services act as repositories for their respective domains: SolutionAnalyzerService manages solution/project access CodeFixProviderFactory manages fix provider instances Factory Pattern CodeFixProviderFactory implements the factory pattern for creating code fix providers: Lazy initialization Caching of instances Dynamic type loading Strategy Pattern DiagnosticFilterService implements filtering strategies: Different filters for severity, IDs, files Composable filter chains Extensible filter types Data Flow Analyzing a Solution 1. MCP Client → AnalyzeSolution tool 2. Tool → SolutionAnalyzerService.AnalyzeSolutionAsync() 3. Service → MSBuildService.CreateWorkspace() 4. Service → Load solution via MSBuildWorkspace 5. For each project: a. Get compilation b. Get diagnostics c. Filter via DiagnosticFilterService d. Aggregate results 6. Return AnalyzeSolutionResponse 7. Tool → Serialize to JSON 8. MCP Server → Return to client Applying Fixes 1. MCP Client → ApplyFixes tool 2. Tool → CodeFixService.ApplyFixesAsync() 3. Service → Load project 4. Service → Get diagnostics for specified IDs 5. Service → CodeFixProviderFactory.GetFixProviders() 6. For each diagnostic: a. Find applicable fix provider b. Get code actions c. Apply changes to solution 7. Service → Generate unified diff 8. Service → Optionally save changes 9. Return ApplyFixesResponse 10. Tool → Serialize to JSON 11. MCP Server → Return to client Workspace Management MSBuildWorkspace Lifecycle Creation: New workspace per operation Configuration: Set up MSBuild properties Loading: Load solution/project Operation: Perform analysis/fixes Cleanup: Dispose workspace Temporary Workspace Pattern For safety, operations use temporary workspaces: Original files never modified directly Changes computed in memory Patches generated for review Explicit save operation required Error Handling Strategy Layered Error Handling Tool Layer: Catches all exceptions, returns JSON error Service Layer: Throws domain-specific exceptions External Layer: Wraps external library exceptions Error Response Format { "error": "Human-readable message", "type": "ExceptionTypeName", "details": { /* optional context */ } } Performance docs/getting-started/basic-usage.html.summary: Basic Usage Learn the fundamentals of using RoselineMCP to analyze and improve your C# code. Overview RoselineMCP provides four main tools: AnalyzeSolution - Analyze entire solutions ListDiagnostics - Get detailed project diagnostics ApplyFixes - Apply automated code fixes CreatePatch - Generate diff patches Quick Examples Analyzing a Solution # Analyze a solution file mcp call analyzeSolution '{ "pathOrGit": "/path/to/MySolution.sln" }' Listing Project Diagnostics # List diagnostics for a specific project mcp call listDiagnostics '{ "project": "MyProject.Core" }' Applying Fixes # Preview fixes without applying mcp call applyFixes '{ "project": "MyProject.Core", "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"], "previewOnly": true }' Creating Patches # Generate a diff patch mcp call createPatch '{ "before": "old code", "after": "new code", "fileName": "Example.cs" }' Understanding Diagnostics Diagnostic IDs RoselineMCP supports various diagnostic ID patterns: CS#### - C# compiler warnings and errors IDE#### - IDE suggestions and refactorings RCS#### - Roslynator analyzer diagnostics SA#### - StyleCop analyzer rules CA#### - Code Analysis rules Severity Levels Diagnostics are categorized by severity: Error - Code that won't compile Warning - Potential issues or bad practices Info - Suggestions for improvement Hidden - Silent diagnostics (usually for IDE features) Filtering Options By Severity Filter diagnostics by minimum severity: { "severity": "warning" // Shows warnings and errors only } By Project Pattern Include or exclude projects by name pattern: { "include": "Core", // Only projects containing "Core" "exclude": "Test" // Exclude projects containing "Test" } By Diagnostic ID Focus on specific diagnostic types: { "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0005"] } By File Pattern Filter by file paths: { "files": ["**/Controllers/**", "**/Services/**"] } Working with Results Solution Analysis Response { "solution": "MySolution.sln", "projects": 5, "diagnosticSummary": { "error": 2, "warning": 45, "info": 12 }, "topDiagnostics": [...] } Diagnostic Details Each diagnostic includes: { "project": "MyProject", "file": "Program.cs", "line": 42, "column": 12, "id": "CS0168", "severity": "warning", "message": "The variable 'x' is declared but never used" } Fix Application Response { "project": "MyProject", "fixesApplied": 12, "filesChanged": ["File1.cs", "File2.cs"], "patch": "--- a/File1.cs\n+++ b/File1.cs\n...", "appliedFixers": [...] } Best Practices 1. Start with Analysis Always analyze first to understand the scope: # Get an overview analyzeSolution --severity warning --maxDiagnostics 50 2. Use Preview Mode Preview fixes before applying: # Preview without changing files applyFixes --previewOnly true 3. Filter Strategically Focus on what matters: # Only production code errors analyzeSolution --exclude "Test" --severity error 4. Apply Fixes Incrementally Fix issues in batches: # Fix one type at a time applyFixes --ids ["CS0168"] # Unused variables applyFixes --ids ["IDE0005"] # Unnecessary usings 5. Document Changes Generate patches for review: # Create a patch for documentation createPatch --fileName "Changes.cs" Integration Examples With Claude Desktop Once configured, you can ask Claude: "Analyze my solution at /path/to/solution.sln" "List all unused variable warnings in MyProject" "Fix all StyleCop issues in the Core project" "Show me what would change if we fix all IDE suggestions" In Scripts Automate analysis in your build pipeline: #!/bin/bash # analyze.sh SOLUTION="/path/to/solution.sln" RESULT=$(mcp call analyzeSolution "{\"pathOrGit\": \"$SOLUTION\"}") if [[ $RESULT == *"\"error\": 0"* ]]; then echo "✅ No errors found" else echo "❌ Errors detected" exit 1 fi In CI/CD Add to your GitHub Actions: - name: Analyze Code run: | dotnet run --project RoselineMCP \ analyzeSolution --path ${{ github.workspace }}/Solution.sln \ --severity error Common Workflows Code Review Preparation Analyze the solution List fixable diagnostics Apply style fixes Generate patch for review Technical Debt Reduction Analyze with all severities Group by diagnostic ID Fix most common issues first Track progress over time Pre-commit Cleanup List diagnostics in changed files Apply automated fixes Review the patch Commit the improvements Troubleshooting No Diagnostics Found Verify the project builds successfully Check if analyzers are installed Try without filters first Fixes Not Applied Ensure the diagnostic ID is fixable Check file permissions Verify no compilation errors Performance Issues Use maxDiagnostics to limit results Filter by specific projects Process in smaller batches Next Steps Your First Analysis - Detailed walkthrough Analyzing Solutions - Advanced techniques API Reference - Complete API documentation

docs/getting-started/first-analysis.html.title: Your First Analysis | RoselineMCP
docs/getting-started/first-analysis.html.summary: Your First Analysis This guide walks you through running your first code analysis with RoselineMCP. Prerequisites Before starting, ensure you have: RoselineMCP installed and configured A C# solution or project to analyze Basic understanding of diagnostic IDs Step 1: Analyze a Simple Solution Let's start with a basic solution analysis: Using MCP Client { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln" } } Understanding the Response You'll receive a response like: { "solution": "YourSolution.sln", "projects": 3, "diagnosticSummary": { "error": 0, "warning": 12, "info": 5, "hidden": 2 }, "topDiagnostics": [ { "project": "YourApp.Core", "file": "Services/DataService.cs", "line": 45, "column": 12, "id": "CS0168", "severity": "warning", "message": "The variable 'ex' is declared but never used" } ] } Step 2: Filter by Severity Focus on the most important issues: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln", "severity": "error", "maxDiagnostics": 20 } } This shows only errors, making it easier to identify critical issues. Step 3: Analyze Specific Projects Target specific parts of your solution: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln", "include": "Core", "exclude": "Test" } } This analyzes only projects containing "Core" in the name, excluding test projects. Step 4: Get Detailed Project Diagnostics Dive deeper into a specific project: { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "YourApp.Core", "max": 50 } } Response Includes Statistics { "project": "YourApp.Core", "totalDiagnostics": 45, "stats": { "byId": { "CS0168": 8, "IDE0005": 12, "RCS1213": 3 }, "bySeverity": { "Warning": 23, "Info": 22 } }, "suggestedFixableIds": ["CS0168", "IDE0005", "RCS1213"], "diagnostics": [...] } Step 5: Preview Fixes Before applying fixes, always preview them: { "tool": "applyFixes", "parameters": { "project": "YourApp.Core", "ids": ["CS0168"], "previewOnly": true } } Review the Patch The response includes a unified diff: --- a/Services/DataService.cs +++ b/Services/DataService.cs @@ -42,7 +42,6 @@ try { return await GetDataAsync(); } catch (Exception ex) { - var unused = ex.Message; _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to get data"); throw; } Step 6: Apply Fixes Once you're satisfied with the preview: { "tool": "applyFixes", "parameters": { "project": "YourApp.Core", "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"], "previewOnly": false } } Complete Workflow Example Here's a complete first analysis workflow: 1. Initial Analysis # Get overview of all issues analyzeSolution --path /src/MySolution.sln 2. Focus on Errors # Check for compilation errors analyzeSolution --path /src/MySolution.sln --severity error 3. List Project Issues # Get detailed diagnostics for main project listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core 4. Preview Fixes # Preview what would be fixed applyFixes --project MyApp.Core --ids CS0168,IDE0005 --previewOnly 5. Apply Fixes # Apply the fixes applyFixes --project MyApp.Core --ids CS0168,IDE0005 Common First-Time Issues Issue: No Diagnostics Found Possible Causes: Solution doesn't have analyzers installed Build errors preventing analysis Incorrect path to solution Solution: # Verify the solution builds dotnet build /path/to/solution.sln # Check for installed analyzers in .csproj <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers" /> Issue: Too Many Diagnostics Solution: Use filtering to focus: { "severity": "error", "maxDiagnostics": 50, "exclude": "Test" } Issue: Fixes Not Available Check fixable IDs: Look at the suggestedFixableIds in the response to see which diagnostics can be automatically fixed. Tips for Beginners Start Small: Begin with a single project rather than entire solution Use Preview: Always preview fixes before applying Fix Incrementally: Fix one diagnostic type at a time Check Severity: Focus on errors first, then warnings Read Messages: Diagnostic messages explain the issues What's Next? Now that you've completed your first analysis: Learn about Analyzing Solutions in depth Explore Listing Diagnostics options Master Applying Fixes safely Understand Creating Patches for review Quick Reference Task Tool Key Parameters Analyze solution analyzeSolution pathOrGit, severity List diagnostics listDiagnostics project, ids Apply fixes applyFixes project, ids, previewOnly Create patch createPatch before, after Getting Help Check the API Reference View Common Diagnostic IDs Review Best Practices

docs/getting-started/installation.html.summary: Installation This guide will help you install and set up RoselineMCP on your system. Prerequisites Before installing RoselineMCP, ensure you have the following: .NET 9.0 SDK or later (Download) MSBuild (included with Visual Studio or .NET SDK) Git (optional, for cloning the repository) Docker (optional, for container deployment) Installation Methods Method 1: Build from Source Clone and build RoselineMCP from source: # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/phmatray/RoselineMCP.git cd RoselineMCP # Restore dependencies dotnet restore # Build the project dotnet build -c Release # Run the application dotnet run --project RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP.csproj Method 2: Docker Container Pull and run the pre-built Docker image: # Pull the latest image docker pull phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest # Run the container docker run --rm -it phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest For specific architectures: # For x64/AMD64 docker pull phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest --platform linux/amd64 # For ARM64 docker pull phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest --platform linux/arm64 Method 3: Direct Integration with Claude Desktop Add RoselineMCP to your Claude Desktop configuration: Locate your Claude Desktop configuration file: macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Linux: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Edit the configuration file and add: { "mcpServers": { "roseline": { "command": "dotnet", "args": [ "run", "--project", "/path/to/RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP.csproj" ] } } } Restart Claude Desktop Verify Installation To verify RoselineMCP is installed correctly: For Command Line # Navigate to the project directory cd RoselineMCP # Run tests dotnet test # Check the build dotnet build --version-suffix test For Docker # Check Docker image docker images phmatray/roseline-mcp # Test run docker run --rm phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest --help Platform-Specific Notes Windows On Windows, you may need to: Enable long path support for deep project structures Run as Administrator for certain MSBuild operations Install Visual Studio Build Tools if not using full Visual Studio macOS On macOS with Apple Silicon (M1/M2): The ARM64 Docker image provides native performance Rosetta 2 can run x64 images if needed Linux On Linux distributions: Install .NET SDK from Microsoft's package repository May need to install additional MSBuild dependencies Ensure Docker daemon is running for container deployment Troubleshooting Common Issues Issue: MSBuild not found # Solution: Install MSBuild locator dotnet tool install -g dotnet-msbuild Issue: NuGet restore fails # Solution: Clear NuGet cache dotnet nuget locals all --clear dotnet restore Issue: Docker permission denied # Solution: Add user to docker group (Linux) sudo usermod -aG docker $USER # Log out and back in for changes to take effect Next Steps Configure RoselineMCP Learn Basic Usage Run Your First Analysis

docs/guides/analyzing-solutions.html.summary: Analyzing Solutions A comprehensive guide to analyzing C# solutions with RoselineMCP. Overview The analyzeSolution tool provides powerful capabilities for analyzing entire C# solutions, identifying code issues, and generating actionable insights. Basic Analysis Simple Solution Analysis { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln" } } Directory-Based Analysis If you have a directory with a single solution: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution/directory" } } Filtering Options By Severity Control which diagnostic levels to include: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "severity": "warning" // Options: error, warning, info, hidden } } Severity Hierarchy: error: Only compilation errors warning: Errors and warnings info: Errors, warnings, and suggestions hidden: All diagnostics including hidden ones By Project Names Include Specific Projects { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "include": "Core|Domain|Services" // Regex pattern } } Exclude Projects { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "exclude": "Test|Mock|Stub" // Regex pattern } } Limiting Results { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "maxDiagnostics": 100 // Default: 100 } } Advanced Scenarios Production Code Analysis Focus on production code with strict severity: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "exclude": "Test|Benchmark|Sample", "severity": "warning", "maxDiagnostics": 200 } } Critical Issues Only Find blocking issues: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "severity": "error", "maxDiagnostics": 50 } } Comprehensive Analysis Full analysis including all severities: { "tool": "analyzeSolution", "parameters": { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/solution.sln", "severity": "hidden", "maxDiagnostics": 500 } } Understanding Results Response Structure { "solution": "YourSolution.sln", "projects": 12, "diagnosticSummary": { "error": 2, "warning": 145, "info": 89, "hidden": 12 }, "topDiagnostics": [ { "project": "YourApp.Core", "file": "Services/UserService.cs", "line": 42, "column": 15, "id": "CS0168", "severity": "warning", "message": "The variable 'ex' is declared but never used" } ] } Key Metrics projects: Total number of projects analyzed diagnosticSummary: Breakdown by severity topDiagnostics: Most important issues (sorted by severity and location) Common Diagnostic IDs Compiler Warnings (CS*) ID Description Severity CS0168 Variable declared but never used Warning CS0219 Variable assigned but never used Warning CS0414 Field assigned but never used Warning CS0649 Field never assigned Warning CS1591 Missing XML documentation Warning CS8600 Possible null reference Warning CS8618 Non-nullable property not initialized Warning IDE Suggestions (IDE*) ID Description Severity IDE0001 Simplify name Info IDE0005 Remove unnecessary imports Info IDE0017 Use object initializers Info IDE0031 Use null propagation Info IDE0051 Remove unused private member Info IDE0059 Remove unnecessary value assignment Info IDE0060 Remove unused parameter Info Roslynator (RCS*) ID Description Severity RCS1001 Add braces Info RCS1018 Add accessibility modifiers Warning RCS1036 Remove redundant empty line Info RCS1089 Use postfix increment/decrement Info RCS1213 Remove unused member declaration Warning StyleCop (SA*) ID Description Severity SA1000 Spacing around keywords Warning SA1101 Prefix local calls with 'this' Warning SA1200 Using directives placement Warning SA1309 Field names must not start with underscore Warning SA1600 Elements should be documented Warning Workflow Examples 1. Progressive Analysis Start broad, then narrow down: # Step 1: Get overview analyzeSolution --path /src/solution.sln # Step 2: Focus on errors analyzeSolution --path /src/solution.sln --severity error # Step 3: Check specific projects analyzeSolution --path /src/solution.sln --include "Core" # Step 4: Deep dive into warnings analyzeSolution --path /src/solution.sln --severity warning --max 200 2. CI/CD Pipeline Analysis # GitHub Actions example - name: Analyze Code Quality run: | RESULT=$(analyzeSolution --path ${{ github.workspace }}/Solution.sln \ --exclude "Test" \ --severity error) if [[ $RESULT == *"\"error\": 0"* ]]; then echo "✅ No errors found" else echo "❌ Errors detected" exit 1 fi 3. Technical Debt Assessment # Comprehensive analysis for technical debt analyzeSolution \ --path /src/LegacyApp.sln \ --severity hidden \ --maxDiagnostics 1000 \ > tech-debt-report.json # Process results cat tech-debt-report.json | jq '.diagnosticSummary' Performance Optimization Large Solutions For solutions with many projects: Filter by project patterns to reduce scope Use severity filters to focus on important issues Limit diagnostics to prevent overwhelming output Process in batches by analyzing project groups Memory Considerations Each project loads into memory during analysis Large solutions may require increased memory Consider analyzing projects individually for very large solutions Troubleshooting No Diagnostics Found Causes: No analyzers installed in projects Build errors preventing analysis All issues filtered out Solutions: <!-- Add to .csproj files --> <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers" Version="8.0.0" /> <PackageReference Include="Roslynator.Analyzers" Version="4.0.0" /> Timeout Issues For large solutions: { "pathOrGit": "/path/to/large-solution.sln", "include": "Priority", // Analyze priority projects first "maxDiagnostics": 50 // Limit initial results } Missing Projects Ensure all projects are properly referenced: # Verify solution file dotnet sln list Best Practices Start with High Severity: Focus on errors first Use Project Filters: Exclude test/sample projects for production analysis Regular Analysis: Run regularly to catch issues early Track Metrics: Monitor diagnostic counts over time Combine with Fixes: Use analysis to identify fixable issues Integration Examples With Claude Desktop "Analyze my solution at /src/MyApp.sln focusing on the Core projects" "Show me all errors in the production code" "What are the top 10 warnings in my solution?" Shell Script #!/bin/bash # analyze-quality.sh SOLUTION_PATH="$1" SEVERITY="${2:-warning}" echo "Analyzing $SOLUTION_PATH..." RESULT=$(analyzeSolution \ --path "$SOLUTION_PATH" \ --severity "$SEVERITY" \ --exclude "Test") ERROR_COUNT=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.diagnosticSummary.error') WARNING_COUNT=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.diagnosticSummary.warning') echo "Found $ERROR_COUNT errors and $WARNING_COUNT warnings" Next Steps Listing Diagnostics - Get detailed project diagnostics Applying Fixes - Fix identified issues Creating Patches - Generate review patches API Reference - Complete API documentation

docs/guides/applying-fixes.html.summary: Applying Fixes Learn how to safely apply automated code fixes with RoselineMCP. Overview The applyFixes tool automatically fixes code issues identified by analyzers. Always preview changes before applying. Basic Usage Preview Mode (Recommended First Step) { "tool": "applyFixes", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": ["CS0168"], "previewOnly": true } } Apply Fixes { "tool": "applyFixes", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"], "previewOnly": false } } Common Fix Scenarios Remove Unused Code { "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0051", "IDE0052", "RCS1213"] } Fix Code Style { "ids": ["SA1101", "SA1200", "SA1210", "SA1309"] } Modernize Code { "ids": ["IDE0017", "IDE0028", "IDE0031", "IDE0041", "IDE0090"] } Understanding the Response { "project": "MyApp.Core", "fixesApplied": 15, "filesChanged": [ "Services/UserService.cs", "Models/Product.cs" ], "patch": "--- a/Services/UserService.cs\n+++ b/Services/UserService.cs\n...", "appliedFixers": [ { "diagnosticId": "CS0168", "fixerName": "Remove Unused Variable", "count": 8 } ] } Safe Fix Workflow List diagnostics to identify fixable issues Preview fixes with previewOnly: true Review the patch to understand changes Apply fixes if satisfied Test your code after applying Best Practices Always preview first Fix one diagnostic type at a time Commit before applying fixes Run tests after fixes Review patches carefully Next Steps Creating Patches Listing Diagnostics API Reference

docs/guides/listing-diagnostics.html.summary: Listing Diagnostics Deep dive into project-level diagnostic analysis with RoselineMCP. Overview The listDiagnostics tool provides detailed diagnostic information for specific projects, including statistics, fixability analysis, and filtering capabilities. Basic Usage List All Diagnostics for a Project { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core" } } Specify Project by Path { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "/path/to/MyApp.Core/MyApp.Core.csproj" } } Filtering Options Filter by Diagnostic IDs Focus on specific diagnostic types: { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0005"] } } Filter by File Patterns Analyze specific parts of your codebase: { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.API", "files": ["**/Controllers/**", "**/Services/**"] } } Combine Filters Use multiple filters together: { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": ["SA1101", "SA1200"], "files": ["**/Models/**"], "max": 50 } } Understanding the Response Complete Response Structure { "project": "MyApp.Core", "totalDiagnostics": 234, "diagnostics": [ { "project": "MyApp.Core", "file": "Services/UserService.cs", "line": 45, "column": 8, "id": "RCS1213", "severity": "warning", "message": "Remove unused member declaration" } ], "stats": { "byId": { "RCS1213": 12, "CS0168": 5, "SA1101": 23, "IDE0005": 8 }, "bySeverity": { "Error": 3, "Warning": 178, "Info": 53 } }, "suggestedFixableIds": [ "CS0168", "IDE0005", "RCS1213", "SA1101" ] } Key Components totalDiagnostics: Total count before limiting diagnostics: Detailed list (limited by max parameter) stats: Statistical breakdown suggestedFixableIds: IDs that can be automatically fixed Advanced Scenarios Finding Unused Code { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": [ "CS0168", // Unused variable "CS0219", // Variable assigned but never used "IDE0051", // Unused private member "IDE0052", // Unread private member "RCS1213" // Unused member declaration ] } } Style Violations { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": [ "SA1000", // Spacing around keywords "SA1101", // Prefix with 'this' "SA1200", // Using directives placement "SA1600" // Elements should be documented ] } } Performance Issues { "tool": "listDiagnostics", "parameters": { "project": "MyApp.Core", "ids": [ "CA1806", // Do not ignore method results "CA1810", // Initialize static fields inline "CA1822", // Mark members as static "CA1827" // Do not use Count when Any can be used ] } } Workflow Examples 1. Incremental Code Cleanup # Step 1: Get overview listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core # Step 2: Identify most common issues # Look at stats.byId to find frequent problems # Step 3: Focus on fixable issues listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \ --ids $(suggestedFixableIds) # Step 4: Target specific files listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \ --files "**/Services/**" \ --ids CS0168,IDE0005 2. Pre-commit Check #!/bin/bash # Check for critical issues before commit RESULT=$(listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core) ERROR_COUNT=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.stats.bySeverity.Error // 0') if [ "$ERROR_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then echo "❌ Found $ERROR_COUNT errors. Please fix before committing." exit 1 fi echo "✅ No errors found. Safe to commit." 3. Technical Debt Tracking # track_debt.py import json import subprocess from datetime import datetime def track_project_debt(project_name): result = subprocess.run( ["listDiagnostics", "--project", project_name], capture_output=True, text=True ) data = json.loads(result.stdout) metrics = { "date": datetime.now().isoformat(), "project": project_name, "total": data["totalDiagnostics"], "by_severity": data["stats"]["bySeverity"], "fixable_count": len(data["suggestedFixableIds"]) } # Save to tracking file with open(f"{project_name}_metrics.json", "a") as f: f.write(json.dumps(metrics) + "\n") return metrics Analyzing Statistics Interpreting byId Stats The stats.byId section shows which diagnostics are most common: "byId": { "SA1101": 45, // Most common - focus on this first "IDE0005": 23, "CS0168": 12, "RCS1213": 8 } Strategy: Fix the most common issues first for maximum impact. Understanding Severity Distribution "bySeverity": { "Error": 0, // Good - no compilation errors "Warning": 45, // Focus area "Info": 120, // Suggestions for improvement "Hidden": 5 // Usually safe to ignore } Fixability Analysis The suggestedFixableIds list shows which issues can be automatically resolved: "suggestedFixableIds": [ "CS0168", // ✅ Can be auto-fixed "IDE0005", // ✅ Can be auto-fixed "SA1101" // ✅ Can be auto-fixed // CS1591 not listed - requires manual documentation ] Integration Patterns With CI/CD # GitHub Actions example - name: Check Code Quality run: | DIAGNOSTICS=$(listDiagnostics --project ${{ matrix.project }}) # Extract metrics TOTAL=$(echo "$DIAGNOSTICS" | jq '.totalDiagnostics') ERRORS=$(echo "$DIAGNOSTICS" | jq '.stats.bySeverity.Error // 0') # Set output echo "total-diagnostics=$TOTAL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT echo "error-count=$ERRORS" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT # Fail if errors if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1 fi With Code Review # Generate report for PR review listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \ --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main) \ > pr-diagnostics.json # Create markdown summary echo "## Diagnostic Report" > report.md echo "Total issues: $(jq '.totalDiagnostics' pr-diagnostics.json)" >> report.md echo "### By Severity" >> report.md jq -r '.stats.bySeverity | to_entries[] | "- \(.key): \(.value)"' pr-diagnostics.json >> report.md Performance Considerations Large Projects For projects with many files: Use file filters to analyze subsets Limit results with max parameter Filter by IDs to focus on specific issues Process in batches for very large codebases Memory Usage Diagnostics are collected in memory Large projects may require more memory Consider splitting analysis by directory Troubleshooting Project Not Found # Verify project exists ls -la *.csproj # Use full path listDiagnostics --project /full/path/to/Project.csproj No Diagnostics Returned # Check if project builds dotnet build MyApp.Core.csproj # Verify analyzers are installed dotnet list package | grep Analyzer Timeout Issues { "project": "LargeProject", "max": 100, // Limit initial results "files": ["**/Priority/**"] // Focus on priority files } Best Practices Regular Analysis: Run weekly to track trends Focus on Fixable: Prioritize suggestedFixableIds Track Metrics: Monitor diagnostic counts over time Incremental Improvement: Fix issues in small batches Combine with ApplyFixes: Use results to guide fixes Quick Reference Common Filter Combinations Goal Parameters Unused code ids: ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0051", "RCS1213"] Style issues ids: ["SA*"] (all StyleCop) Performance ids: ["CA1806", "CA1822", "CA1827"] Specific directory files: ["**/Services/**"] Fixable only Use suggestedFixableIds from response Next Steps Applying Fixes - Fix the issues found Creating Patches - Generate review patches Analyzing Solutions - Solution-wide analysis API Reference - Complete API documentation
